sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 34.8% a year, from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5.93 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].
Growth slowed from 64.2% in FY2021 to 0.1% in FY2023, before recovering to 10.6% in FY2025 [D218][D311][D406].
FY2017 operating margin of -422.5% [F22] reflects stock-based compensation of $2.64 billion [X82], tied mainly to the CEO award and RSUs vesting on the IPO [P74].
Operating margin improved 15.7pp in FY2024 [D371], as R&D fell $219.2 million on lower stock-based compensation and headcount [P35].
Advertising Revenue added 5.3pp and Other Revenue added 5.4pp to FY2025 revenue growth of 10.6% [D538][D545][D406].
Other revenue rose $287.6 million, mainly from higher subscription revenue as subscribers grew [P24][S42].
Advertising revenue rose $282.4 million on impressions up about 17%, partly offset by cost per impression down about 10% [P24][S39].
Other Revenue's share of revenue rose from 4.3% in FY2023 to 12.6% in FY2025, while Advertising fell to 87.4% [D539][D543][D536].
Revenue growth beat operating-cost growth by 5.5pp in FY2025, an incremental operating margin of 44.8% [D430][D429].
FY2025 operating margin of -9.0% is the window high, against a median of -32.4% and a low of -422.5% [F30][D554][D555][D553].
The FY2025 margin bridge shows cost of revenue adding 1.1pp, R&D adding 1.3pp and other lines adding 3.3pp [D431][D432][D433].
Within other lines, sales and marketing fell $42.4 million on event timing and lower advertising investment [P22][D433].
Net margin of -7.8% sits above operating margin of -9.0% because other income of $68.9 million included $96.7 million of debt extinguishment gains [F50][F30][X130][P18].
Because that gain does not recur, the FY2025 net margin overstates underlying progress compared with operating margin [F50][F30][P18].
Operating cash flow of $656.2 million and free cash flow of $437.2 million contrast with a net loss of $460.5 million [F80][F100][F40].
Stock-based compensation of $1.02 billion, equal to 155.0% of operating cash flow, is the main non-cash add-back [X90][D396][P13].
Capex of $219.0 million was 3.7% of revenue and 1.34x D&A, mostly for leased-facility improvements [F90][D392][D395][P10].
Net debt reached $596.3 million in FY2025, up from $267.6 million in FY2024 and from net cash of $1.44 billion in FY2021 [D399][D351][D211].
Net cash was -10.1% of revenue, in the 0th percentile of five internet peers, whose median is 45.0% [D400][D578][D579].
The current ratio of 3.56x is the lowest in the window, against a median of 5.15x [F180][D565][D567].
Buybacks of $750.9 million were 171.7% of free cash flow, yet diluted shares still rose 2.1% [X156][D402][D425].
Net losses ran for all ten years, with FY2025 at $460.5 million, though the loss shrank 34.0% [R1][F40][D408].
Stock-based compensation was 17.1% of revenue in FY2025 and above 10% in each of nine years, equal to 191.1% of the operating loss [R2][D390][D404].
Net cash has turned to net debt over four straight years, reaching $596.3 million, while interest expense rose from $21.6 million to $122.0 million [R3][D399][X99][X100].
The interest jump came mainly from the 2033 and 2034 Notes issued in 2025 [P19][X100].
Buybacks exceeded free cash flow in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, reaching 171.7% in FY2025 [R4][D402].
Free cash flow margin holding at or above 7.4% would confirm the improvement, while a fall toward FY2024's 4.1% would reverse it (FY2026 10-K) [D393][D345].
Operating margin better than -9.0% would extend the recovery, while a slide back to FY2024's -14.7% would reverse it (FY2026 10-K) [F30][F29].
Net debt wider than $596.3m, with buybacks again above the 171.7% of free cash flow, would signal more strain (FY2026 10-K) [D399][D402].
